notes_context:
Memory items from past tasks:
- [rb-0011] Apply approval threshold to support-initiated money moves: Finance policy FIN-2026-03 requires a second approver for refunds/credits above 500.00, enforced via keyword-only approved_by.
  Add `*, approved_by=None` to refund/credit signatures and raise BillingError("approval_required") when the rounded amount exceeds 500.00 and approved_by is falsy. Amounts at or below the threshold must still work without an approver, so keep the parameter optional and keyword-only.
- [rb-0001] Round monetary results with the project's money helper: The first attempt returned an unrounded Decimal division and was rejected because the team requires ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent).
  When a function returns a money value, wrap the final computation in the repository's round_money helper rather than returning a raw Decimal or using Python's round()/quantize(), which use banker's rounding. Check ledgerly/money.py for the canonical helpers (ZERO, to_money, round_money) and reuse them.
- [rb-0008] Compute periodic occurrences with floor division plus one: The renewal index was computed as (after - start) // length + 1, which correctly yields the first occurrence strictly after `after` including the boundary case.
  For 'first event strictly after t' with events at start + n*period, use n = (t - start) // period + 1. Handle t < start separately by returning start + period, since the start itself is not a renewal.
- [rb-0004] Reuse existing error codes and validation patterns from sibling modules: Matching the codebase's established BillingError codes and money-normalization helpers makes new functions consistent and passes hidden tests.
  Before implementing a new function, grep sibling modules for similar validation (e.g. payments.authorize) and reuse their error codes ('invalid_state', 'non_positive_amount') and helpers (round_money, to_money, ZERO). Mirror the exact state-check message format used elsewhere.
- [rb-0010] Check idempotency before state validation: Team convention requires idempotency_key to be checked first, before any state or amount validation, so replays return the original result instead of raising errors.
  At the top of any money-moving function, scan audit.events(<event_type>) for a matching idempotency_key and return the original record immediately. Do this before validating payment status or amounts, otherwise a retried call on an already-refunded payment raises invalid_state instead of returning the prior result.
- [rb-0002] Read the money module before implementing financial logic: The agent only discovered round_money after the review comment, though it was already imported in invoice.py.
  Before writing any arithmetic on prices or totals, inspect the existing money utilities and sibling functions (e.g. line_total, invoice_total) to mirror their rounding and conversion conventions. Existing imports in the target file are a strong hint about required helpers.

item.title: Reuse existing money helpers for rounding and coercion
item.description: When implementing monetary functions, reuse the project's to_money/round_money helpers instead of raw float math or round().
item.content: Inspect ledgerly/money.py and sibling modules (invoice.py) first; they define to_money, round_money, ZERO. Coerce inputs with to_money and round results with round_money so Decimal precision and cent rounding match the rest of the codebase.

item.title: Match the project's error type and code conventions
item.description: Raise the domain-specific BillingError with a short machine-readable code rather than ValueError or a bare exception.
item.content: Read ledgerly/errors.py to learn the BillingError(code, message) signature and existing code strings (e.g. invalid_state, negative_amount). For new validation, pick a consistent snake_case code like invalid_rate and pass the offending value as the message.

item.title: Verify edge cases with a quick script before submitting
item.description: After implementing, run the test suite plus a small ad-hoc script exercising boundaries and type coercions.
item.content: Run pytest, then manually check boundary values (0 and 100 inclusive), out-of-range rejection, and string/Decimal inputs. This catches rounding and validation gaps that hidden tests likely probe.
